title: Cocceius with Wittich: faith a species of love — vs those who keep love only as effect
source_text: XXXIX. Et Wittichius ipse loco supra citato in confirmationem sententiae suae profert verba Coccei, dum viveret, in Academia Leydensi Professoris. Fides illa, inquit, est species amoris Dei, cum diligo Deum ut expiantem peccata, & sanantem a peccati morbo & foetu, ut sim ad gloriam ejus. Ad ultima Mosis, pag. 396. Et alio in loco, Omnino igitur fides cum charitate connexa est, cum & ipsa fides nihil sit, nisi charitatis Christi effusio in cordibus nostris, & ejus sensus & reciprocatio. Jam amat qui credit; & nisi amet, nec credit. In Examine Apologiae, pag. 209. Sed contra sentiunt multi e Theologis Reformatis, ut Samuel Maresius, Robertus Baronius, Bucanus, & denique quotquot fidem in solo intellectu locant, ut Petrus Molinaeus, & Professores Salmurienses. Nam omnes illi docent quidem Dei amorem ex vera fide nasci, & esse effectum ab ea plane inseparabilem, nolunt tamen esse actum a fide elicitum, quoniam hoc esset fidem cum charitate confundere.
pass_a_gloss: And Wittich himself in the place cited above, in confirmation of his opinion, brings forward the words of Cocceius, while he lived Professor in the Academy of Leiden. That faith, he says, is a species of the love of God, when I love God as expiating sins, and healing from the disease and offspring of sin, that I may be unto His glory. On the Last Things of Moses, page 396. And in another place: Altogether therefore faith is connected with charity, since faith itself also is nothing but the pouring out of the charity of Christ in our hearts, and its sense and reciprocation. Now he who believes loves; and unless he loves, he does not believe. In the Examination of the Apology, page 209. But many of the Reformed Theologians feel otherwise, as Samuel Maresius, Robert Baron, Bucanus, and finally as many as locate faith in the intellect alone, as Peter du Moulin and the Professors of Saumur. For all those indeed teach that love of God is born from true faith, and is an effect plainly inseparable from it, yet they will not have it be an act elicited by faith, since that would be to confuse faith with charity.
pass_b_english: Wittich cites Cocceius: faith = a species of love of God as expiator and healer.
Faith connected with charity — Christ’s charity poured in the heart; who believes loves.
Opposed: Maresius, Baron, Bucanus, du Moulin, Saumur — faith in intellect alone.
They grant love is born from true faith and inseparable as effect — but not an act elicited as faith itself (lest faith = charity).
